title: CSTB May Day march against hunger, high prices and working/living conditions
location: Cotonou; from Étoile Rouge toward Bourse du Travail
scope: One May Day march followed by a labor meeting in Cotonou; the two opened reports refer to the same CSTB event, not independent events.
organizer: Confédération Syndicale des Travailleurs du Bénin (CSTB)
participants_original: La Flamme describes a very large turnout ('place noire du monde', 'sortie massive', 'masses mobilisées') but gives no count; its politically aligned organizer perspective may inflate size.
threshold_50_evidence: Qualitative evidence supports at least 50: La Flamme's opened account describes the square as black with people and a massive turnout and reports people joining from multiple social sectors. It provides no numeric count, and the publication's PCB alignment / organizer proximity warrants caution; exact bounds remain unknown.

start_date.summary: Both opened La Flamme and Daabaaru articles report a CSTB May Day march on 1 May 2023.

location.summary: Opened reports place the march in Cotonou, starting at Étoile Rouge and ending at the Bourse du Travail; search-only April notice stated this planned route.

organizer.summary: The opened reports identify the Confédération Syndicale des Travailleurs du Bénin (CSTB) as organizer; the April notice also announced the event.

demands.summary: The accounts describe claims concerning hunger, cost of living, employment/working conditions, political detainees and press freedom; the advance notice expressly directs the march's grievances to the government.

participants_original.summary: La Flamme uses qualitative mass-turnout language, but provides no number; treat the scale description cautiously because of its PCB alignment and proximity to the organizer.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The opened La Flamme account says the square was black with people, describes a massive turnout and reports several social sectors joining; this qualitative evidence supports the threshold, but no numeric bounds are available and source perspective may inflate.

protester_violence.summary: unknown; neither opened account reports violence by march participants.

state_response.summary: unknown; the opened reports do not describe an event-specific state response.

notes: S001 and S002 report the same CSTB event; they are not counted as independent confirmation of turnout. Attendance threshold is supported qualitatively by S001 only, with explicit source-bias caveat; no exact estimate. S004 is a search-only advance notice, not proof of occurrence.
open_questions: Could an independent contemporaneous source corroborate scale or attendance?
What response, if any, did state authorities make to this specific march?
